notes.title: Project Alpha PRD
notes.content:
Product Requirements Document: Project Alpha
Version: 2.1 | Last updated: 2026-02-28
Owner: Tina Rodriguez | Eng Lead: Mike Torres

## Overview
Project Alpha is TechFlow's flagship AI productivity assistant — an intelligent workspace that learns from user behavior to surface relevant context, automate repetitive tasks, and reduce tool-switching.

## Target Users
- Knowledge workers at companies with 50-500 employees
- Product managers, engineers, designers who use 5+ tools daily

## Core Features (v1 - March 15 launch)
1. Smart Context Panel — surfaces relevant docs, messages, and tasks based on current focus
2. AI Summarization — one-click meeting notes and document summaries
3. Cross-tool Search — unified search across Slack, Notion, GitHub, Google Workspace
4. Action Suggestions — proactive task recommendations based on patterns

## Technical Requirements
- Response time: <200ms for context panel
- Accuracy: >90% relevance for surfaced items
- Privacy: all processing on-device for free tier, cloud-optional for enterprise
- Integrations: Slack, Notion, GitHub, Google Calendar, Jira (v1)

## Launch Plan
- Beta: Feb 15 (internal) → Feb 28 (50 external users)
- Public: March 15 (Product Hunt + press)
- Enterprise: March 30 (Acme Corp first customer)

## Open Questions
- Pricing for enterprise tier (Rachel working on this)
- Whether to include calendar integration in v1 or push to v1.1
- Mobile app timeline (Derek's designs not finalized)

notes.title: Competitive Analysis
notes.content:
Competitive Landscape — AI Productivity Tools (Updated Feb 2026)

## Direct Competitors

1. Notion AI
- Strengths: Large user base, integrated workspace, good AI features
- Weaknesses: Slow, limited cross-tool, no real-time context
- Pricing: $10/user/month (AI add-on)
- Threat level: HIGH

2. Glean
- Strengths: Enterprise search, strong integrations, Series C funded
- Weaknesses: Expensive ($50/user/month), slow deployment, no consumer play
- Pricing: Enterprise only, $50+/user/month
- Threat level: MEDIUM (different market segment)

3. Mem
- Strengths: AI-first, good UX, fast
- Weaknesses: Small team, limited integrations, no enterprise
- Pricing: $15/user/month
- Threat level: MEDIUM

4. Rewind AI
- Strengths: On-device, privacy-first, screen recording
- Weaknesses: Mac only, creepy factor, limited actionability
- Pricing: $20/month individual
- Threat level: LOW

## Our Differentiation
- Cross-tool intelligence (not just search)
- Proactive context (not reactive queries)
- Privacy-first architecture (on-device for free tier)
- Enterprise-ready from day one (SOC2, SSO)
- Speed: <200ms response time vs. competitors' 1-2 seconds

notes.title: Calendar Integration Spec
notes.content:
Calendar Integration — Technical Specification
Version: 1.0 | Owner: Tina Rodriguez

## Overview
Integrate with Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook to provide:
- Pre-meeting context (relevant docs, previous notes, attendee info)
- Post-meeting AI summaries
- Smart scheduling suggestions
- Calendar-aware notifications

## Supported Providers
1. Google Calendar (via Google Workspace API)
2. Microsoft Outlook (via Microsoft Graph API)
3. Apple Calendar (stretch goal, Q3)

## Data Model
- Events: title, time, attendees, location, description
- Recurring patterns: weekly 1:1s, standups, team meetings
- Context links: associated documents, Slack channels, Jira tickets

## Privacy
- Read-only calendar access (never write without explicit permission)
- Attendee info limited to name + email (no profile enrichment)
- All calendar data encrypted at rest
- Enterprise: optional on-premise calendar connector

## Timeline
- Google Calendar: March 8 (in Alpha v1)
- Outlook: April 15 (v1.1)
- Apple Calendar: July (stretch)

notes.title: Pricing Experiments Results
notes.content:
Pricing Experiment Results — Feb 2026

Experiment: Tested 4 pricing tiers with 200 waitlist users via fake door test

Variant A: $10/month individual, $15/user/month team
Variant B: $15/month individual, $20/user/month team
Variant C: Free tier + $20/month pro + $50/user/month enterprise
Variant D: Usage-based ($0.10/query after 100 free queries/month)

Results:
- Variant C won (32% higher intent-to-purchase)
- Free tier drives adoption (78% said free tier important)
- Enterprise buyers insensitive to price below $60/seat/year
- Usage-based confused users (lowest intent)

Recommendation:
- Free: 100 queries/day, 3 integrations, single user
- Pro ($15/month): unlimited queries, all integrations, 5 team members
- Enterprise ($50/seat/year): SSO, SOC2, admin controls, unlimited everything

Next steps:
- Confirm with Rachel (enterprise pricing alignment)
- Build billing infrastructure (Stripe integration)
- A/B test landing page with final pricing

notes.title: A/B Test Results — Onboarding Flow
notes.content:
A/B Test Results: Onboarding Flow Optimization
Test period: Feb 1–14, 2026 | N = 847 new signups

Control (A): 5-step wizard (connect tools → set preferences → tutorial → invite team → start)
Variant (B): 2-step quick start (connect 1 tool → start immediately, optional setup later)

Results:
- Activation rate: A = 52%, B = 71% (+19 percentage points, p < 0.01)
- Day 7 retention: A = 38%, B = 44% (+6pp, p < 0.05)
- Tools connected (day 7): A = 2.8, B = 2.1 (users connect more later in A)
- Time to first value: A = 4.2 minutes, B = 1.1 minutes

Decision: Ship Variant B (quick start)
- Users who see value quickly connect more tools over time
- Reduced onboarding friction is worth the initial lower tool connection
- Add contextual prompts to connect additional tools after first 'aha' moment

Design implications for Derek:
- Simplify onboarding to 2 screens
- Add 'Connect more tools' nudge in settings after day 2

notes.title: Design Review with Derek
notes.content:
Design Review — Mobile App Concepts
Date: 2026-02-25
Attendees: Tina, Derek

Derek presented 3 concepts for mobile app:

Concept A: 'Command Center'
- Bottom tab navigation (Search, Notifications, Meetings, Capture)
- Floating AI button for voice queries
- Pros: familiar pattern, discoverable features
- Cons: too many tabs, feels generic

Concept B: 'Flow'
- Single scrolling feed with AI-curated content
- Swipe gestures for actions (archive, snooze, star)
- Pros: simple, engaging, unique
- Cons: learning curve, less discoverable

Concept C: 'Smart Cards'
- Card-based UI with contextual stacks
- Meeting cards expand to show prep materials
- Pros: information density, contextual
- Cons: complex interaction model

Decision: Hybrid of A + C
- Tab navigation for structure (from A)
- Card-based content display (from C)
- Voice AI button from A

Next steps:
- Derek to produce high-fidelity mockups by March 10
- Share with Alex for technical feasibility review
- User test with 5 beta participants

notes.title: Product FAQ
notes.content:
TechFlow AI — Product FAQ (Internal + External)

Q: What is TechFlow?
A: TechFlow is an AI productivity assistant that connects your work tools and surfaces relevant context automatically.

Q: Which tools does TechFlow integrate with?
A: Slack, Notion, GitHub, Google Calendar, Jira (v1). More coming in Q2-Q3 2026.

Q: Is my data safe?
A: Yes. Free tier processes everything on-device. Enterprise tier offers SOC2 compliance, SSO, and optional data residency controls.

Q: How much does TechFlow cost?
A: Free tier available. Pro: $15/user/month. Enterprise: contact sales.

Q: Can I use TechFlow on mobile?
A: Mobile app coming Q2 2026. Currently desktop (Mac, Windows, Linux).

Q: How is TechFlow different from Notion AI?
A: TechFlow works across all your tools, not just one workspace. It proactively surfaces context rather than requiring you to ask.

Q: What about enterprise security?
A: SOC2 Type I certified. SSO via SAML/OIDC. Admin controls, audit logs, and data residency options available.

Q: Can I try before buying?
A: Yes! Free tier has no time limit — 100 queries/day, 3 tool integrations.

notes.title: API Rate Limiting Strategy
notes.content:
API Rate Limiting — Design Decision

Problem: Third-party APIs (Slack, GitHub, Google) have rate limits that affect our cross-tool search.

Current limits:
- Slack: 50 req/min (Web API), 1 req/sec (Events API)
- GitHub: 5000 req/hr (authenticated)
- Google Calendar: 500 req/100sec/user
- Notion: 3 req/sec

Strategy:
1. Aggressive caching: Cache responses for 5 min (configurable per tool)
2. Request batching: Combine multiple user queries into batch API calls
3. Graceful degradation: If rate limited, serve from cache with staleness indicator
4. Priority queue: Real-time search gets priority over background sync
5. Per-user budgets: Distribute rate limits fairly across concurrent users

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1: Redis-based cache layer (Mike, Sprint 24)
- Phase 2: Smart batching algorithm (Tom, Sprint 25)
- Phase 3: User-facing rate limit indicators (Derek, Sprint 25)

Metrics to track:
- Cache hit rate (target: >80%)
- P99 response time under rate limiting (<500ms)
- User-visible errors from rate limits (<0.1%)

notes.title: Onboarding Optimization Notes
notes.content:
Onboarding Optimization — Learnings & Next Steps

Current funnel (from A/B test):
- Signup → Connect first tool: 71% (after switching to 2-step)
- Connect first tool → First search: 83%
- First search → Day 1 return: 64%
- Day 1 return → Day 7 active: 44%

Biggest drop-off: Day 1 → Day 7 (need habit formation)

Hypotheses to test:
1. Daily email digest showing 'what you missed' increases D7 retention
2. Push notification for 'your meeting in 30 min — here's context' drives reopens
3. Team invite reduces churn (accountability + shared value)

Planned experiments:
- March 18: Email digest experiment (Nina helping with copy)
- March 25: Push notification experiment (need mobile or browser notifs)
- April 1: Team referral flow experiment

Target: Improve D7 retention from 44% to 55% by end of Q2

notes.title: Customer Feedback — Enterprise Pain Points
notes.content:
Enterprise Customer Pain Points — Synthesis from Sales Calls
Source: Rachel's deal notes + my customer calls (Feb 2026)

Top 5 enterprise blockers:

1. SECURITY COMPLIANCE (100% of enterprise prospects)
- SOC2 required by all
- Some need ISO 27001 (larger enterprises)
- HIPAA for healthcare vertical (future)

2. SSO/IDENTITY (90% of enterprise prospects)
- Okta most common (60%)
- Azure AD (30%)
- OneLogin, Ping (10%)

3. ADMIN CONTROLS (80%)
- Who can connect which tools
- Data access policies
- Usage reporting for IT

4. DATA RESIDENCY (50%)
- US-only storage for US companies
- EU storage option needed for GDPR
- Some need on-premise (government, finance)

5. INTEGRATION DEPTH (70%)
- Not just search — need to create/update
- Jira: create tickets from AI suggestions
- Slack: post summaries to channels
- Custom integrations via API

Implication for roadmap:
- SOC2 + SSO must be in v1 enterprise
- Admin dashboard is Q2 priority
- Data residency is Q3 (requires infra work)
- Deep integrations can be gradual (API-first approach)
